passage:
I'm Yamini, Vaibhav's younger sister, and I was the one the hospital called at 1 am. He had skidded his scooter into a divider on the ring road. A cracked wrist and stitches above his eye, the doctor said. Lucky.
When Papa walked into the ward, he didn't shout. He just stood at the foot of the bed and cried, which I had never seen him do.
For two years Vaibhav had said the drinking was "just weekends", "just stress", "under control". That night he said none of it. He stared at the plaster on his wrist and whispered, "I could have killed someone." Then, "I can't stop, Yamu. I've tried."
He looked more scared and more tired than I had ever seen him. I don't know exactly what was going on inside him. But I knew the door was open, maybe only for tonight. I sat on the bed and said, "Okay. Then we get help. Tomorrow. Together."

qa.a: A cracked wrist and stitches above his eye.

qa.a: Papa is likely shaken by fear of what could have happened and grief at seeing his son hurt, with any anger held back behind the tears.

Friday, 5 March. Keerthana's manager called her into the glass cabin. The third missed client meeting, the late mornings, the smell. "We're letting you go." She argued: it was the new project, the traffic, anyone would be tired. At home she told Sahil it was office politics and opened a bottle.
Sunday, 7 March. She woke on the sofa at noon and found Sahil at the table with the bank statements, very quiet. "We can't pay rent next month," he said. "And I found the bottles in the shoe rack." She started to say, "It's not—" and stopped. Her hands were shaking. She was so tired of explaining.
Monday, 8 March. She sat on the edge of the bed, frightened in a way she couldn't name. "Sahil, I think I have a problem. A real one."
He put his arm around her. "Thank you for saying it. Let's call someone today, before either of us talks ourselves out of it."

What was Keerthana feeling on Monday when she finally spoke?
qa.a: She was frightened in a way she couldn't name and exhausted by explaining, so her denial gave way to admitting a real problem.

qa.a: He senses the opening may not last, so acting before either of them talks themselves out of it turns her honesty into real help.

qa.q: What might Sahil have been going through on Sunday at the table?
qa.a: Sahil was facing unpaid rent and hidden bottles, likely feeling scared and hurt, and very quiet rather than ready to shout.

grounding: Illustrates a firing and a partner's discovery cracking a young woman's denial about drinking over three days, and a supportive reaction to her admission.
